name: prefix-cache-speed

config.PREFIX_CACHE: on (cache-on runs) and off (cache-off decode runs)

tests.filter: cold, first sighting, shared prefix, warm at 4,096, 12,288 and 32,768 tokens, 3 reps, every cell its own stream: no cold reply served from the cache, every shared and warm reply a hit
prefix_snapshot_costs (median of 5 after a discarded run, at 4 lengths)

commands: for i in 1 2 3; do ./inkling2mini.sh bench decode; done   (cache on)

PREFIX_CACHE=off ./inkling2mini.sh memwatch begin; PREFIX_CACHE=off ./inkling2mini.sh start; for i in 1 2 3; do PREFIX_CACHE=off ./inkling2mini.sh bench decode; done; ./inkling2mini.sh memwatch report; ./inkling2mini.sh stop

NODE=node-3 LAB_SRC=<engine worktree> PKG=gb-model TEST_ENV='REXL3_INKLING2_LOOP_DIR=/home/spark/models/Inkling-2-Mini-SAGE-REXL3-4.23bpw' scripts/ops_dev.sh test inkling2_loop_prefix prefix_snapshot_costs
notes: The cold-vs-cached prompts of cache_ttft.py each have their own filler stream: a first version shared leading blocks between sizes and its 12K and 32K 'first sighting' cells read partial hits (4,032 and 12,224 cached tokens); the tool was fixed (lanes 1000+) and the run recorded is the second one. The decode workload sends prefix_cache false, so the on/off decode comparison measures the presence of the cache, not a hit. Cache-off boot saw 1 GiB more free memory than the cache-on boot (free_after 102.45 vs 101.45 GiB, the planner's whole-GiB quantisation); the KV plan is the same in both (4,100 pages).
